opening_message:
Ticket 1: Richard Davis (employee ID E011) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E011.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write, and Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Richard Davis (E011) is a contractor with basic security training (note this differs from the earlier note claiming full-time). Contractors never get admin; write requires advanced training. Since he has basic training, max access is read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Richard Davis (E011) requested write access to Payroll. The notes conflict on employment type: one claims full-time Payroll Specialist, but the Security DB explicitly states he is a contractor with basic security training and flags the discrepancy. Under policy, contractors get read, or write only with advanced security training, and never admin. With basic training, his maximum access is read. Since the requested write exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum: read.
